status: Meets the Bench Standard bar on Opus and Haiku: 62/63 on both in the final round, well ahead of no skill (36/63 Opus, 34/63 Haiku), never behind on the four traps, and no invented rules, sources, banned words or examples in any with-skill output. Caveat: replies occasionally miscount by one (eight contractions where there are nine, a 39-word post that measures 38). There is no public comparison skill to compare against.
method: 9 evals (4 traps), expectations written before any run. Round 1 ran the skill and no skill on Haiku and Opus in fresh headless agents, graded blind by a separate Opus grader. No comparison skill exists locally, so no comparison-skill config ran. One expectation (eval 1 spelling: 'colour' and 'cancelled' fit UK as well as Canadian) was clarified after round 1 because the grader showed it rewarded an assumption; eval 1 was regraded for every config under the clarified wording. Rounds 2 and 3 re-ran the skill as it was revised (round 3 on Haiku and Opus).
losses_and_open_issues: Round 3, Haiku eval 3: confirmed a Website rule that rests on one page of evidence (should be provisional)
Round 3, Opus eval 4: one new rule carried both confirmed and provisional statuses

Round 1, Haiku eval 1: confirmed 'calm, not loud' from the rejected draft's general note; Haiku eval 4 dismissed Hannah's 'your bookkeeper' to 'our team' edit as compatible instead of asking; Haiku eval 2 confirmed the brand name; Haiku eval 8 didn't end on the approval question (all fixed in 1.1.0)
Round 2, Haiku eval 7: named three of four untagged rules (fixed in 1.2.0)
Miscounts in replies, not invented facts: Opus eval 9 says eight contractions (there are nine) in rounds 1 and 3; both eval 2 runs in round 3 call a 38-word post 39 words
No expectation tests that a pattern seen in three approved samples is marked confirmed; Opus tends to confirm such rules, Haiku tends to keep them provisional
Replies sometimes mention how other tools read the file (Opus eval 7), despite the rule against it

Without the skill: no-skill Opus invented banned words ('customers, clients, users', 'eliminate'), credited rules to Mailchimp and rewrote voice.md anyway, edited claims.md and BRAND.md unasked; no-skill Haiku asserted Canadian spelling with words not in the samples and settled a contradicted exclamation rule
Every with-skill run left the user's evidence files unchanged; Check and Guided runs wrote nothing to brand/
